content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Combine a request, routine fact, past event, and future plan clearly. Model: “I usually shop every Friday. Yesterday I went late, so tomorrow I am going early.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use a1 everyday challenge clearly and politely. One useful response is: “I usually shop every Friday. Yesterday I went late, so tomorrow I am going early.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where a1 everyday challenge is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?

listening.question: What is the speaker going to do tomorrow?

pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Contrast YESTERday and toMORrow; stress the time words. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Contrast YESTERday and toMORrow; stress the time words.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about a1 everyday challenge.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using a1 everyday challenge; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise a1 everyday challenge?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: I usually shop every Friday. Yesterday I went late, so tomorrow I am going early.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about a1 everyday challenge with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about a1 everyday challenge. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: I usually shop every Friday. Yesterday I went late, so tomorrow I am going early. Submit your draft first.
